clue.text: Bishop outside another empty church

parts.note: ex is a Latin-derived prefix meaning out of or outside

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A bishop stands outside yet another church that has no congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' strips 'another' to its outer letters, AR.
explanation.definitionFit: An exarch is a senior bishop in the Eastern Orthodox churches, ranking above a metropolitan.

clue.text: Force Jeff, not Jack, to overcome cold collecting Bill

indicators.note: in a down clue, to overcome is to sit on top of, so the first piece goes above the next
Jeff with no Jack means the name loses its J, as 'not' asks

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: collecting means taking another piece inside itself

parts.note: icy means very cold
AC (account) is a bill

explanation.surface: Someone forces Jeff, rather than Jack, to beat a cold while picking up a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overcome' places the first part on top in this down clue, and 'collecting' means the cold word holds the bill inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Efficacy is effectiveness, the power or force to produce an intended result.

clue.text: Loss of smell from influenza I'm so narked about

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the extracted letters are read backwards
from signals that the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by flu complains it has robbed them of their sense of smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes AIMSONA out of 'influenzA I'M SO NArked'; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Anosmia is the medical term for a loss of the sense of smell, a known symptom of some viral infections.

clue.text: Craic that somehow is providing a release

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters reach their final form by some unexplained rearrangement

explanation.surface: Irish-style fun and banter, it is claimed, offers a welcome emotional release.
explanation.walkthrough: Craic is Irish for lively fun and conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cathartic gives a purging release of pent-up emotion.

clue.text: Fellows mingling with Nationalist politicians for a drink

indicators.note: mingling means mixing together, so the combined letters are jumbled

parts.note: chaps are fellows, men
the SNP, the Scottish National Party, is a party of nationalist politicians

explanation.surface: A group of men socialise with Scottish nationalist politicians over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The SNP is the Scottish National Party; CHAPS and SNP are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong distilled spirit, a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Catch sailors with rum heartlessly changing seasonal hymn

indicators.note: changing means altering the order of the letters
losing its heart, rum keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Sailors are caught drinking rum and changing the words of a festive hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' reduces 'rum' to RM, which joins CATCH SAILORS before 'changing' mixes them.
explanation.definitionFit: A carol sung at Christmas is a hymn for the festive season.

clue.text: Discovered snack shop supplies a single hot chip

indicators.note: dis-covered means uncovered, the outer letters removed from each word

explanation.surface: A snack shop is found to be serving just one hot chip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' strips the outer letters from SNACK and SHOP, leaving NAC and HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is one tortilla chip, served hot with melted cheese, one of a plate of nachos.

clue.text: One overworked approaching Christmas, but sack is never far away

definitions.text: One overworked approaching Christmas, but sack is never far away

parts.words: One overworked approaching Christmas, but sack is never far away
parts.note: the sack suggests dismissal from a job, but it is really the bag of letters and parcels carried on the rounds during the festive rush

explanation.surface: A worker under seasonal strain fears dismissal is always looming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' hints at being fired; it is actually a mailbag, always to hand for this busy worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail carriers are run off their feet in the weeks of cards and parcels before Christmas.

clue.text: Vision of what tennis pro hopes to achieve having day off

indicators.note: having something off means it is taken away

parts.words: what tennis pro hopes to achieve
parts.note: a tennis professional hopes to be seeded, earning a seeding in a tournament draw

explanation.surface: A tennis player takes a day off while dreaming of success.
explanation.walkthrough: A seeding ranks top players so they avoid each other early in a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing is the faculty of sight, so it means vision.

clue.text: Spoilsport that could disrupt nativity play

definitions.meaning: a person who selfishly stops others enjoying what they themselves cannot use
a nativity play stages the birth of Jesus in a manger, so an animal in it could spoil the show

explanation.surface: A killjoy who might wreck a school nativity play.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from Aesop's fable of a dog that lay in the cattle's hay, which it could not eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names someone who spitefully keeps from others what is of no use to themselves.

clue.text: Windsor, say, bears Royal crest and cross over main entrance

indicators.note: bears means carries, so the first piece holds the next inside it

parts.note: Windsor is the name of a typeface, an example of a font

indicators.note: a crest is the top of something, so only the first letter is taken
over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix in a church

explanation.surface: Windsor, the royal house, displays its crest and a cross over the palace entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windsor, say' suggests the royal family but means a typeface. 'crest' takes the top letter of Royal, and 'over' turns the cross word round.
explanation.definitionFit: The front door of a house is its principal entrance.

clue.text: Husband escaping from modest social class

indicators.note: escaping from means getting out of, so the letter is removed

parts.note: chaste means pure and modest

explanation.surface: A husband flees a modest social class.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, as in the traditional Hindu system.

clue.text: Scotsman rejected standard island apéritif

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Mac is a stock name for a Scotsman
par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: A Scotsman turns down an ordinary island drink before dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Campari is a bitter Italian liqueur typically drunk before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Frosty for example in Leeds, now Manchester

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Frosty weather is reported in Leeds, and now in Manchester too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frosty' looks like weather but is a name; the letters sit in 'LeedS NOW MANchester'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frosty is the title figure of the Christmas song about a figure made of packed snow.

clue.text: Song starts off copying hymn, adapting normal tune

indicators.note: the starts of the following words, their first letters, are taken off

explanation.surface: A song begins by copying a hymn, adapting a familiar tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A chant is a simple song or melody, often sung to repeated words.

clue.text: Inviting time to pour out mostly gin cocktail

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to empty is to pour out the contents

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: It is tempting, at this hour, to pour out most of a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts EMPTY to EMPT; 'cocktail' rearranges GIN to ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tempting is attractive, so it is inviting.

clue.text: Virtuoso conductor in action, excited about finale to Proms

indicators.note: about means around, so the mixed letters surround the next piece
excited means agitated, stirred up, so the letters are mixed
the finale is the end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A great conductor is excitedly in action at the end of the Proms season.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are London's summer concert series. 'excited' mixes IN ACTION to TOCANINI, which goes 'about' S.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian conductor, famous for his virtuosic command of the orchestra.

clue.text: Academically challenged group of pupils positioned close together

parts.note: thick is an informal word for slow-witted
a set is a group of pupils of similar ability taught together

explanation.surface: A class of struggling pupils is seated close together.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a set is a class grouped by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset can describe things planted or placed densely, close to one another, like a hedge.

clue.text: Nutty biscuits

definitions.meaning: nutty in the slang sense of mad or crazy
thin crisp savoury biscuits, often eaten with cheese

explanation.surface: Biscuits containing nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for mad and the name for plain crisp biscuits.

clue.text: Reportedly understood Xmas message — maybe footballers would dispute it?

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so the words are spoken

parts.note: read in its past tense means understood; a card carries a Christmas greeting

explanation.surface: Someone apparently got the Christmas message, and footballers might argue with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Past-tense 'read' is said like 'red'.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee shows the red card to send a player off, and players often protest it.

clue.text: Cut down tree, prioritising shape initially before length

indicators.note: before means placed in front of what follows
prioritising means putting the preceding pieces first, ahead of the tree
initially means at the start, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A tree is felled, its shape considered before its length.
explanation.definitionFit: To slash prices or budgets is to reduce them sharply.

clue.text: Extravagant caviare brings excessive desire for wealth

indicators.note: extravagant means wild, going beyond bounds, so the letters stray

explanation.surface: Lavish caviare spending shows greed for riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is greed, an extreme longing for money and possessions.

clue.text: Disgust from article on practice pervading North America

indicators.note: the outer piece is spread through by the inner one, so the inner sits inside it
in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
use means habit or practice

explanation.surface: Revulsion arises from an article on a custom spreading across North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea can mean strong revulsion, not just sickness.

clue.text: Occasionally candid journalist describes new adult supplements

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is taken
describes in the sense of drawing a line around, enclosing the next piece

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the crossword journalist
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: An outspoken journalist now and then writes about new supplements for adults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' takes every other letter of candid; 'describes' means the journalist encloses N.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are additions to a book or document, items supplementing the main text.

clue.text: See 29
Spies old woman adopting extremes of altogether revolting language …

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old woman

indicators.note: the extremes are the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Spies hear an old woman using thoroughly disgusting language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like 'disgusting' but turns round CIAMARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic tongue, spoken in the Near East in biblical times.

clue.text: … to scold son, given delay receiving money essentially

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: a lag is a delay

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letter

explanation.surface: The old woman continues, scolding her son for a delay over money.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue; MONEY's middle letter is N.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal use, to slang someone is to abuse or berate them.

clue.text: Praises endlessly tenor that is visiting Gloucestershire

indicators.note: visiting means calling in on, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: Glos is the standard abbreviation for the English county of Gloucestershire

indicators.note: endlessly means without its ends, the first and last letters lost

parts.note: tenor in the sense of general meaning or drift

explanation.surface: Someone keeps praising a tenor who is visiting Gloucestershire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tenor' is not the singer but the gist, DRIFT, trimmed to RIF.
explanation.definitionFit: To glorify is to extol or praise highly.

clue.text: Examination, hourly with odd intervals, relating to hearing

parts.note: an audit is an official examination of accounts

indicators.note: the odd letters are the gaps left out, so the even letters are taken

explanation.surface: An exam held every hour, with odd breaks, tests the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditory is the adjective for things concerned with the sense of hearing.

clue.text: Unusual tinsel thing, regular feature of carol service

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters take an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd bit of tinsel is always seen at the carol service.
explanation.definitionFit: This German-born Christmas carol is sung at almost every carol service.
